claims.claim: In V3C-seq, samples are digested and ligated under conditions that favor intramolecular interaction, and the resultant novel virus-cell DNA fragments are subjected to high-throughput sequencing.
claims.source: Samples are then digested and ligated under conditions that favor intramolecular interaction, and the resultant novel virus-cell DNA fragments are subjected to high-throughput sequencing (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is a description of the V3C-seq methodology shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The V3C assay provides a precise genomic map of the sites with which viral DNA interacts.
claims.source: The assay provides a precise genomic map of the sites with which viral DNA interacts, and the frequency with which unique individual linked fragments are generated provides quantification of these interactions.
claims.evidence: This describes the output of the V3C-seq assay.

claims.claim: The frequency with which unique individual linked fragments are generated in V3C-seq provides quantification of virus-cell interactions.
claims.source: The assay provides a precise genomic map of the sites with which viral DNA interacts, and the frequency with which unique individual linked fragments are generated provides quantification of these interactions.
claims.evidence: This describes the quantitative aspect of the V3C-seq assay.

claims.claim: By 12 hr post-infection and release (representing approximately 4–6 hr into S-phase), MVM genomes associated with discrete regions on most cellular chromosomes.
claims.source: Clustering algorithms and visualization of interaction sites on the UCSC Genome Browser (Kent et al., 2002; Ramírez et al., 2016) revealed that by 12 hr post-infection and release (representing approximately 4–6 hr into S-phase) MVM genomes associated with discrete regions on most cellular chromosomes [Figure 2—figure supplements 1B and 2, (Kent et al., 2002)].
claims.evidence: This is shown in the V3C-seq data presented in Figure 2—figure supplements 1B and 2.

claims.claim: Cellular sites of MVM association served as initial amplification points for MVM, and upon progression to 16 hpi, the virus both expanded at these regions and associated with new sites.
claims.source: These cellular sites served as initial amplification points for MVM, and upon progression to 16 hpi, the virus both expanded at these regions and associated with new sites (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the time-course V3C-seq data in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The clusters of MVM interacting sites on each chromosome ranged in density and in size from approximately 1–2 Mb to larger 5–15 Mb-size domains.
claims.source: The clusters of interacting sites on each chromosome ranged in density and in size (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), from approximately 1–2 Mb to larger 5–15 Mb-size domains (chromosomes 17 and 19 are shown in Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is observed in the V3C-seq data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: While most chromosomes contained multiple small VADs, many contained 1–3 larger VADs of 5–15 Mb size.
claims.source: While most chromosomes contained multiple small VADS, many contained 1–3 larger VADs of 5–15 Mb size.
claims.evidence: This is observed in the V3C-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Chromosomes 1, 13, 18, X and Y had fewer discernible MVM interaction sites.
claims.source: Chromosomes 1, 13, 18, X and Y had fewer discernible interaction sites.
claims.evidence: This is observed in the V3C-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Approximately 51% of VADs identified at 12 hpi were retained at 16 hpi.
claims.source: Comparison of MVM interaction sites across the entire mouse genome showed that approximately 51% of VADs identified at 12 hpi were retained at 16 hpi, indicating that approximately 84% of VADs identified at 16 hpi were newly generated (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the V3C-seq data and shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Approximately 84% of VADs identified at 16 hpi were newly generated.
claims.source: Comparison of MVM interaction sites across the entire mouse genome showed that approximately 51% of VADs identified at 12 hpi were retained at 16 hpi, indicating that approximately 84% of VADs identified at 16 hpi were newly generated (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the V3C-seq data and shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Approximately 39% of MVM interaction sites detected at 16 hpi were retained at 20 hpi.
claims.source: Approximately 39% of MVM interaction sites detected at 16 hpi were retained at 20 hpi, while only approximately 18% of the interaction sites identified at 20 hpi were newly generated (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the V3C-seq data and shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Only approximately 18% of the MVM interaction sites identified at 20 hpi were newly generated.
claims.source: Approximately 39% of MVM interaction sites detected at 16 hpi were retained at 20 hpi, while only approximately 18% of the interaction sites identified at 20 hpi were newly generated (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the V3C-seq data and shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Clustering analysis of MVM interaction sites in multiple replicates over the time-course of infection showed that they were reproducible across replicates.
claims.source: Clustering analysis of MVM interaction sites in multiple replicates over the time-course of infection showed that they were reproducible across replicates (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: MVM interaction sites clustered together at 16 and 20 hpi in a characteristic manner that was distinct from early (12 hpi) and late (24 hpi) infection.
claims.source: Importantly, MVM interaction sites clustered together at 16 and 20 hpi in a characteristic manner that was distinct from early (12 hpi), and late (24 hpi) infection.
claims.evidence: This is shown in the clustering analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: MVM interaction with the host chromosome increased as infection progressed.
claims.source: These results suggested that interactions of MVM with the cellular chromosome increased as infection progressed.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the time-course V3C-seq data.

claims.claim: By 24 hpi, MVM interaction with the host chromosome was extensive.
claims.source: By 24 hpi, MVM interaction with the host chromosome was extensive (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the V3C-seq data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: At late times of infection (24 hpi), in the presence of saturating amount of MVM DNA, interactions of the viral genome with sites throughout the mouse genome were observed.
claims.source: Additionally, at these late times, in the presence of saturating amount of MVM DNA, we observed interactions of the viral genome with sites throughout the mouse genome.
claims.evidence: This is observed in the V3C-seq data at 24 hpi shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: VADs identified earlier during infection featured properties that enabled viral recruitment and replication.
claims.source: This further suggested that VADs identified earlier during infection featured properties that enabled viral recruitment and replication.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that early VADs are specific while late infection shows widespread interaction.

claims.claim: The cellular genome undergoes substantial DNA damage by late stages of MVM infection.
claims.source: It is noteworthy, however, that the cellular genome undergoes substantial DNA damage by late stages of infection (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and as described below), likely precluding detection of some interactions effectively by V3C-seq.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and discussed in the text.

claims.claim: Viral packaging would be expected to reduce available viral genomes by approximately 20 hpi.
claims.source: In addition, viral packaging would be expected to reduce available viral genomes by approximately 20 hpi (Cotmore and Tattersall, 2014), which would also be predicted to contribute to the decreased interaction seen at 20 hpi in Figure 2B.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on known parvovirus biology, supported by citation.

claims.claim: MVM association with the VAD at 19qA was readily detectable using Taqman-based 3C-qPCR assays.
claims.source: MVM association with the VAD at 19qA was readily detectable in our standard protocol using Taqman probes complementary to the MVM genome (forward) and the cellular genomic site (reverse) (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D using 3C-qPCR validation.

claims.claim: MVM association with the 19qA VAD was substantially diminished either in the absence of intramolecular ligation, or when cross-links were reversed prior to intramolecular ligation.
claims.source: This association was substantially diminished, either in the absence of intramolecular ligation, or when cross-links were reversed prior to intramolecular ligation (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2D as a control experiment.

claims.claim: MVM associations with cellular VADs were specific and mediated by DNA-DNA and/or DNA-protein intramolecular crosslinks.
claims.source: These experiments defined the lower limit of background levels generated by our V3C assay, and suggested that MVM associations with cellular VADs were specific, and mediated by DNA-DNA and/or DNA-protein intramolecular crosslinks.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the control experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Focused 3C-qPCR in parasynchronized NIH-3T3 fibroblasts infected with MVMp showed association with a subset of the VADs identified in A9 cells.
claims.source: Focused 3C-qPCR in parasynchronized NIH-3T3 fibroblasts infected with MVMp (Figure 2E), and EL4 lymphocyte cells infected with the lymphotrophic variant MVMi (Figure 2F) both showed association with a subset of the VADs identified in A9 cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), which suggested a common mechanism may exist for the establishment of MVM replication sites in these mouse cell lines.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2E using 3C-qPCR in NIH-3T3 cells.

claims.claim: Focused 3C-qPCR in EL4 lymphocyte cells infected with the lymphotrophic variant MVMi showed association with a subset of the VADs identified in A9 cells.
claims.source: Focused 3C-qPCR in parasynchronized NIH-3T3 fibroblasts infected with MVMp (Figure 2E), and EL4 lymphocyte cells infected with the lymphotrophic variant MVMi (Figure 2F) both showed association with a subset of the VADs identified in A9 cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), which suggested a common mechanism may exist for the establishment of MVM replication sites in these mouse cell lines.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 2F using 3C-qPCR in EL4 cells.

claims.claim: A common mechanism may exist for the establishment of MVM replication sites in different mouse cell lines.
claims.source: Focused 3C-qPCR in parasynchronized NIH-3T3 fibroblasts infected with MVMp (Figure 2E), and EL4 lymphocyte cells infected with the lymphotrophic variant MVMi (Figure 2F) both showed association with a subset of the VADs identified in A9 cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), which suggested a common mechanism may exist for the establishment of MVM replication sites in these mouse cell lines.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that VADs are conserved across different cell types.

claims.claim: V3C-seq is a valid means to map the interaction of a lytic linear DNA virus with specific sites on the host cell genome.
claims.source: Together, we interpret our results as establishing that V3C-seq is a valid means to map the interaction of a lytic linear DNA virus with specific sites on the host cell genome.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the validation experiments and reproducibility of the V3C-seq data.

claims.claim: Mock infected A9 cells (taken 12 hr post release) showed a significant number of sites of DNA damage, as identified by γ-H2AX, as they passed into S-phase.
claims.source: Mock infected A9 cells (taken 12 hr post release, hpr) showed a significant number of sites of damage, as identified by γ-H2AX, as they passed into S-phase.
claims.evidence: This is shown in the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Sites of DNA damage in mock infected cells were likely ERFs (early-replicating fragile sites), which accrue damage during replication.
claims.source: These were likely ERFs, which accrue damage during replication (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation based on the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data and known biology of ERFs.

claims.claim: Approximately 55% of the γ-H2AX sites identified in mock infected cells overlapped with those identified at 16 hr post-infection.
claims.source: Whole-genome peak analysis of all γ-H2AX bound regions revealed that approximately 55% of the sites identified in mock infected cells overlapped with those identified at 16 hr post-infection (hpi); approximately 55% of sites identified at 16 hpi were newly generated (Figure 3B, peak calling using EPIC and intersection using BEDtools, (Quinlan and Hall, 2010), as described in Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data and shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Approximately 55% of γ-H2AX sites identified at 16 hpi were newly generated.
claims.source: Whole-genome peak analysis of all γ-H2AX bound regions revealed that approximately 55% of the sites identified in mock infected cells overlapped with those identified at 16 hr post-infection (hpi); approximately 55% of sites identified at 16 hpi were newly generated (Figure 3B, peak calling using EPIC and intersection using BEDtools, (Quinlan and Hall, 2010), as described in Materials and methods).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data and shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: By 16 hpi, sites of DNA damage concentrated in distribution and expanded in number.
claims.source: By 16 hpi, sites of damage concentrated in distribution, and expanded in number (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: At 16 hpi, MVM had begun to induce additional sites of DNA damage, as evident both by ChIP-seq and increased tail moments in Comet assays.
claims.source: At this point in infection MVM had begun to induce additional sites of DNA damage, as evident both by ChIP-seq and increased tail moments in Comet assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is shown by γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data and Comet assay data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: The majority of γ-H2AX-containing sites at 20 hpi were newly generated, coinciding with only 10% of the sites identified at 16 hpi.
claims.source: The majority of γ-H2AX-containing sites at 20 hpi were newly generated, coinciding with only 10% of the sites identified at 16 hpi, indicating the widespread induction of DNA damage by this point of infection.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: By 20 hpi, there was widespread induction of DNA damage.
claims.source: The majority of γ-H2AX-containing sites at 20 hpi were newly generated, coinciding with only 10% of the sites identified at 16 hpi, indicating the widespread induction of DNA damage by this point of infection.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data.

claims.claim: The γ-H2AX ChIP-seq regions identified at 16 hpi correlated well with γ-H2AX ChIP-seq performed following 12 hr treatment with HU.
claims.source: Interestingly, the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq regions identified at 16 hpi correlated well with γ-H2AX ChIP-seq performed following 12 hr treatment with HU (Figures 3A and 16 hpi vs HU).
claims.evidence: This is shown by comparison of γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Approximately 51% of γ-H2AX peaks detected 16 hpi were shared with those induced after 12 hr treatment with HU.
claims.source: Approximately 51% of γ-H2AX peaks detected 16 hpi were shared with those induced after 12 hr treatment with HU, and conversely, approximately 26% of the peaks identified following treatment with HU were shared at 16 hpi.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Approximately 26% of the γ-H2AX peaks identified following treatment with HU were shared at 16 hpi.
claims.source: Approximately 51% of γ-H2AX peaks detected 16 hpi were shared with those induced after 12 hr treatment with HU, and conversely, approximately 26% of the peaks identified following treatment with HU were shared at 16 hpi.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: At 12 hpi, MVM associated with approximately 55% of sites that in mock infected cells exhibited DNA damage upon progression into S-phase.
claims.source: At 12 hpi, MVM associated with approximately 55% of sites that in mock infected cells exhibited DNA damage upon progression into S-phase.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: By 16 hpi, MVM association with sites that exhibited DNA damage in mock infected cells rose to close to 80%.
claims.source: By 16 hpi, this association rose to close to 80%.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: By 16 hpi, close to 90% of γ-H2AX occupied sites overlapped with VADs.
claims.source: By 16 hpi, close to 90% of γ-H2AX occupied sites overlapped with VADs (Figure 3C), which included γ-H2AX sites present in uninfected cells (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: By the late time point of 20 hpi, approximately 70% of the γ-H2AX sites co-localized with VADs.
claims.source: By the late time point of 20 hpi, approximately 70% of the γ-H2AX sites co-localized with VADs.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: MVM association with damaged sites increased from 16 hpi to 20 hpi.
claims.source: Visualization of MVM association in the vicinity of γ-H2AX-positive sites using hierarchical clustering further revealed that MVM association with damaged sites increased from 16 hpi to 20 hpi; however, increased incidence of cellular DNA breaks after 20 hpi led to a decrease in the proportion of MVM-associated damaged sites (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the heatmap analysis in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Increased incidence of cellular DNA breaks after 20 hpi led to a decrease in the proportion of MVM-associated damaged sites.
claims.source: Visualization of MVM association in the vicinity of γ-H2AX-positive sites using hierarchical clustering further revealed that MVM association with damaged sites increased from 16 hpi to 20 hpi; however, increased incidence of cellular DNA breaks after 20 hpi led to a decrease in the proportion of MVM-associated damaged sites (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the heatmap analysis in Figure 3D and is an interpretation of the data.

claims.claim: Approximately 25% of the VADs identified at 12 hpi associated with the γ-H2AX sites identified following 12 hr of treatment with HU.
claims.source: Notably, approximately 25% of the VADs identified at 12 hpi, and approximately 95% of VADs identified at 16 hpi, associated with the γ-H2AX sites identified following 12 hr of treatment with HU.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Approximately 95% of VADs identified at 16 hpi associated with the γ-H2AX sites identified following 12 hr of treatment with HU.
claims.source: Notably, approximately 25% of the VADs identified at 12 hpi, and approximately 95% of VADs identified at 16 hpi, associated with the γ-H2AX sites identified following 12 hr of treatment with HU.
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Randomly generated peaks showed less than 1% overlap with γ-H2AX peaks identified 16 hpi.
claims.source: Randomly generated peaks showed less than 1% overlap with γ-H2AX peaks identified 16 hpi (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is shown as a control analysis in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The strong correlation of MVM interaction sites with sites that in uninfected cells exhibit DNA damage upon replication is consistent with the notion that MVM may have initially established replication at cellular fragile sites that are susceptible to DNA damage as cells cycle through S-phase.
claims.source: The strong correlation of MVM interaction sites with sites that in uninfected cells exhibit DNA damage upon replication is consistent with the notion that MVM may have initially established replication at cellular fragile sites that are susceptible to DNA damage as cells cycle through S-phase, although it cannot be formally ruled out that these sites were virally-induced at the earliest times in infection.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation between V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data.

claims.claim: It cannot be formally ruled out that the sites of MVM association at early times were virally-induced.
claims.source: The strong correlation of MVM interaction sites with sites that in uninfected cells exhibit DNA damage upon replication is consistent with the notion that MVM may have initially established replication at cellular fragile sites that are susceptible to DNA damage as cells cycle through S-phase, although it cannot be formally ruled out that these sites were virally-induced at the earliest times in infection.
claims.evidence: This acknowledges a limitation in definitively determining causality.

claims.claim: VADs correlated strongly with γ-H2AX ChIP-seq sites identified on cellular chromosomes of non-infected, HU-treated A9 cells.
claims.source: It is also important to note that VADs also correlated strongly with γ-H2AX ChIP-seq sites identified on cellular chromosomes of non-infected, HU-treated A9 cells (Figure 3A, red rectangles).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A by comparison of V3C-seq and HU-treated γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data.

claims.claim: The correlation of VADs with HU-induced damage sites strongly implied that the γ-H2AX identified associated with MVM during infection resides on cellular DNA.
claims.source: This strongly implied, although does not prove, that the γ-H2AX identified associated with MVM during infection resides on cellular DNA.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation with HU-induced damage.

claims.claim: Sites of damage in uninfected cells, sites of damage induced by virus, and sites of damage induced by treatment of the DNA-damaging agent HU overlap significantly.
claims.source: It is striking that sites of damage in uninfected cells, sites of damage induced by virus, and sites of damage induced by treatment of the DNA-damaging agent HU overlap so significantly.
claims.evidence: This is an observation based on the γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data comparisons.

claims.claim: BRCA1 binds DNA and can co-localize with γ-H2AX in DNA double-strand break repair foci, although typically in a more narrow pattern.
claims.source: Cellular sites of DNA damage also often contain BRCA1, which binds DNA and can co-localize with γ-H2AX in DNA double-strand break repair foci, although typically in a more narrow pattern (Barlow et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about BRCA1, supported by citation.

claims.claim: VADs strongly associated with sites identified by BRCA1 ChIP-seq at 16 hr post-infection.
claims.source: As expected, VADs also strongly associated with sites identified by BRCA1 ChIP-seq at 16 hr post-infection (Figure 4A, row 2).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A by comparison of V3C-seq and BRCA1 ChIP-seq data.

claims.claim: VADs overlapped with BRCA1 and γ-H2AX sites in primary mouse cells induced with replication stress agents and characterized as ERFs in previously published studies.
claims.source: Furthermore, VADs also overlapped with BRCA1 and γ-H2AX sites in primary mouse cells induced with replication stress agents (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B), and characterized as ERFs, in previously published studies (Barlow et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B, with citation to Barlow et al., 2013.

claims.claim: MVM can infect transformed human cells.
claims.source: As MVM can infect transformed human cells, we also performed focused V3C-qPCR at 16 hpi in parasynchronized SV40-transformed human NB324K cells.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about MVM host range.

claims.claim: In human NB324K cells at 16 hpi, MVM localized to the previously characterized human fragile site FRA5H, but not FRA11F.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, MVM localized to the previously characterized human fragile site FRA5H, but not FRA11F.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C using 3C-qPCR in human cells.

claims.claim: In human NB324K cells at 16 hpi, MVM associated weakly with the prototypical human fragile site, FRA3B.
claims.source: MVM also associated weakly at this time point with the prototypical human fragile site, FRA3B.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C using 3C-qPCR in human cells.

claims.claim: ChIP-seq for the MVM-NS1 protein was performed as an indirect confirmation of MVM recruitment to the cellular genome.
claims.source: As an indirect confirmation of MVM recruitment to the cellular genome, we performed ChIP-seq for the MVM-NS1 protein, which binds covalently to the viral genome, and non-covalently to additional ACCAACCA consensus sequences throughout the MVM genome (Christensen et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: This is described as a validation approach, with citation to Christensen et al., 1995.

claims.claim: MVM-NS1 binds covalently to the viral genome and non-covalently to additional ACCAACCA consensus sequences throughout the MVM genome.
claims.source: As an indirect confirmation of MVM recruitment to the cellular genome, we performed ChIP-seq for the MVM-NS1 protein, which binds covalently to the viral genome, and non-covalently to additional ACCAACCA consensus sequences throughout the MVM genome (Christensen et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NS1 binding, supported by citation.

claims.claim: ChIP-seq assays for NS1 would confirm cellular sites associated with the viral DNA by secondary crosslinking of NS1-bound MVM DNA to cellular DNA.
claims.source: We reasoned that ChIP-seq assays for NS1 would confirm cellular sites associated with the viral DNA by secondary crosslinking of NS1-bound MVM DNA to cellular DNA.
claims.evidence: This is the rationale for performing NS1 ChIP-seq.

claims.claim: NS1 binding profiles to cellular chromosomes 17 and 19 are concordant with the VADs at 16 hpi.
claims.source: Figure 4A shows NS1 binding profiles to cellular chromosome 17 and 19 that are concordant with the VADs at 16 hpi, further validating our findings from V3C-seq assays.
claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A by comparison of NS1 ChIP-seq and V3C-seq data.

claims.claim: Approximately 90% of the peaks identified by NS1-, BRCA1-, and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq overlapped with VADs identified by V3C.
claims.source: A genome-wide analysis of called peaks indicated that approximately 90% of the peaks identified by NS1-, BRCA1 -, and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq overlapped with VADs identified by V3C (Figure 4B and C), while overlap was undetectable when intersected with a randomly generated library of ChIP-seq peaks of equivalent size (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is quantified from comparison of ChIP-seq and V3C-seq data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claims.claim: Overlap between ChIP-seq peaks and VADs was undetectable when intersected with a randomly generated library of ChIP-seq peaks of equivalent size.
claims.source: A genome-wide analysis of called peaks indicated that approximately 90% of the peaks identified by NS1-, BRCA1 -, and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq overlapped with VADs identified by V3C (Figure 4B and C), while overlap was undetectable when intersected with a randomly generated library of ChIP-seq peaks of equivalent size (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is shown as a control analysis in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: The binding profile of NS1, BRCA1 and γ-H2AX around a VAD site at 16 hpi centered within 1 Mb of the MVM associated cellular site.
claims.source: In concordance with these findings, the binding profile of NS1, BRCA1 and γ-H2AX around a VAD site at 16 hpi centered within 1 Mb of the MVM associated cellular site (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is shown in the heatmap analysis in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: V3C-seq and ChIP-seq experiments are consistent with a model that upon infection, MVM first localized to cellular sites susceptible to DNA damage as cells progressed into S-phase, and as infection progressed, localized to additional sites of damage that were virally induced, to amplify its replication.
claims.source: Taken together, our V3C-seq and ChIP-seq experiments are consistent with a model that upon infection, MVM first localized to cellular sites susceptible to DNA damage as cells progressed into S-phase, and as infection progressed, localized to additional sites of damage that were virally induced, to amplify its replication.
claims.evidence: This is the main model proposed based on all the V3C-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claims.evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C and D using 3D-FISH microscopy.

claims.claim: The median distance between the MVM genome and the 15qE-VAD probe was approximately 0.6 µm.

claims.evidence: This is quantified from 3D-FISH measurements shown in Figure 5E.

claims.source: In contrast, non-VAD control sites on chromosome 12 and 17 (12qA3 and 17qA2) exhibited a much greater range of co-location and were separated from its nearest MVM genome by median distances of 1.1 and 1.1 µm, respectively.

results.result: A novel high-throughput Viral Chromosome Conformation Capture assay (V3C-seq) was developed and validated for mapping genome-wide interactions between a lytic virus genome and the cellular chromosome. The assay uses formaldehyde crosslinking, digestion, intramolecular ligation, and high-throughput sequencing to provide precise genomic maps and quantification of virus-cell interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C38, C39, C55-C58, and C82 collectively describe the development and validation of V3C-seq with supporting experimental data throughout the manuscript (Figures 2-6). The methodology is clearly described, validated by multiple approaches (3C-qPCR, microscopy, CRISPR experiments), and shown to be reproducible across replicates (C68). Control experiments (C77, C78) demonstrate specificity of the assay.

results.result: Upon infection, MVM initially associated with sites of cellular DNA damage that in mock-infected cells also exhibited DNA damage as cells progressed through S-phase. At 12 hpi, MVM associated with approximately 55% of sites showing DNA damage in mock-infected cells, rising to close to 80% by 16 hpi.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C41, C83-C84, C94-C95, and C103 are supported by V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data showing overlap between MVM association sites (VADs) and DNA damage sites in mock-infected cells (Figures 2 and 3). Quantitative analysis demonstrates ~55% overlap at 12 hpi increasing to ~80% at 16 hpi (Figure 3C). The interpretation that these are likely ERFs (C84) is reasonable given the timing and known biology.

results.result: As MVM infection progressed, new DNA damage sites were induced, and the virus subsequently associated with these newly induced sites to amplify infection. Approximately 84% of VADs at 16 hpi were newly generated, and DNA damage sites expanded in number and concentrated in distribution over the infection time course.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C8, C44, C60, C64-C65, C70, C86-C90 are supported by time-course V3C-seq and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data (Figures 2 and 3). The data show progressive expansion of both VADs and DNA damage sites, with quantitative analysis demonstrating that ~84% of VADs at 16 hpi are newly generated (C65, Figure 2C). ChIP-seq data confirm increasing DNA damage over time (C87-C90), and Comet assays provide independent validation (C88, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).

results.result: Sites of MVM association identified biochemically by V3C-seq were confirmed microscopically using 3D-FISH and super-resolution microscopy. The median distance between MVM and VAD probes (19qA and 15qE) was approximately 0.6-0.7 μm, similar to the median radius of APAR bodies, while non-VAD control sites showed significantly greater distances (~1.1 μm).
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C122-C128 are supported by 3D-FISH and super-resolution microscopy data (Figure 5). Quantitative distance measurements show close localization between MVM and VAD probes (0.6-0.7 μm) compared to non-VAD controls (1.1 μm), with statistical significance (Figure 5E). The distances are consistent with the median radius of APAR bodies, supporting the interpretation that VAD sites coincide with APAR bodies (C126).

results.result: MVM can be targeted specifically to artificially induced sites of DNA damage, demonstrated by both laser micro-irradiation and CRISPR/Cas9-induced DNA breaks. MVM and NS1 co-localized with laser-induced DNA damage stripes, and CRISPR/Cas9-induced breaks at chromosome 9 resulted in substantially increased MVM-cellular DNA interactions at the break site without affecting pre-existing VADs.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C42, C129-C131, C133-C139 are supported by laser micro-irradiation experiments (Figure 6A) and CRISPR/Cas9 experiments (Figure 6B-G). Both approaches demonstrate that MVM can be recruited to artificially induced DNA damage sites. The CRISPR experiments include appropriate controls showing no effect on pre-existing VADs (C137, C139), and reciprocal validation using both 3C-qPCR and ChIP-qPCR (C136, C138).

results.result: MVM-associated sites (VADs) overlap significantly with previously identified topologically-associated domains (TADs), with VADs occupying multiple adjacent TADs, suggesting that several adjacent TADs may contain the necessary environment to support MVM expression and replication.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C178, and C179 are supported by comparison of V3C-seq data with published Hi-C data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-D). The overlap between VADs and TADs is clearly demonstrated, and the observation that VADs span multiple adjacent TADs is evident in the data. The interpretation that multiple TADs may provide supportive environment (C179) is reasonable but remains somewhat speculative.

results.result: MVM established replication at cellular DNA damage sites, which provide replication and expression machinery. The proposed model suggests that MVM first homes to sites of pre-existing endogenous DNA damage to initiate infection, then spreads to newly induced damage sites to amplify infection.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C43, and C121 represent the main interpretive model of the study, supported by the collective evidence from V3C-seq, ChIP-seq, microscopy, and artificial DNA damage experiments (C1-C5). The model is consistent with all experimental observations, though the authors acknowledge that specific localization of input genomes remains circumstantial (C196, C197). The model is well-supported but represents an interpretation rather than direct demonstration.

results.result: Super-resolution microscopy (Airyscan and GSD-STORM) demonstrated that γ-H2AX and FANCD2 localized to the periphery of APAR bodies at 16 hpi, suggesting that MVM replication centers localize to and expand adjacent to sites of cellular chromatin undergoing DNA damage.
results.evaluation: Claims C47, C50, C51, and C54 are supported by super-resolution microscopy data (Figure 1C-D). The peripheral localization of DDR markers relative to APAR bodies is clearly shown, and quantitative distance measurements support close association (Figure 1B). The interpretation that MVM replication centers localize adjacent to damaged cellular chromatin (C54) is reasonable given the microscopy data and the known size of γ-H2AX platforms (C52).

results.result: γ-H2AX ChIP-seq regions at 16 hpi correlated well with those induced by 12 hr hydroxyurea (HU) treatment. Approximately 51% of γ-H2AX peaks at 16 hpi were shared with HU-induced peaks, and approximately 95% of VADs at 16 hpi associated with HU-induced γ-H2AX sites, strongly implying that γ-H2AX associated with MVM resides on cellular DNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C93, C100-C101, C105-C107 are supported by comparison of γ-H2AX ChIP-seq data from infected cells, mock-infected cells, and HU-treated cells (Figure 3A-C). The quantitative overlap analysis is rigorous, and the striking overlap between infection-induced, replication-induced, and HU-induced damage sites (C107) supports the interpretation that γ-H2AX resides on cellular DNA (C106). However, the authors appropriately note this does not definitively prove the location (C106, C192, C193).

results.result: VADs strongly associated with sites identified by BRCA1 and NS1 ChIP-seq at 16 hpi. Approximately 90% of peaks identified by NS1, BRCA1, and γ-H2AX ChIP-seq overlapped with VADs, with binding profiles centered within 1 Mb of MVM-associated cellular sites, providing independent validation of V3C-seq results.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C110, C114-C120 are supported by ChIP-seq data for BRCA1 and NS1 (Figure 4A-C). The ~90% overlap between ChIP-seq peaks and VADs is substantial and statistically significant compared to random controls (C119). The concordance between NS1 ChIP-seq and V3C-seq (C117) provides strong validation, as NS1 is covalently bound to viral DNA (C115). The heatmap analysis showing centered binding profiles (C120) further supports the specificity of the associations.

results.result: V3C-seq results were validated by focused 3C-qPCR in multiple cell types. MVM association with VADs was detected in A9, NIH-3T3, and EL4 cells, with association substantially diminished in control conditions (no ligation or reversed crosslinks), suggesting a common mechanism for MVM replication site establishment across mouse cell lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C81 are supported by 3C-qPCR validation experiments (Figure 2D-F). The controls (C77) demonstrate specificity of the assay, and detection of VADs in multiple cell types (C79-C80) supports generalizability. The inference of a common mechanism (C81) is reasonable given the conservation of VADs across cell types, though the mechanism itself is not elucidated.

results.result: By 12 hpi, MVM genomes associated with discrete regions on most cellular chromosomes, ranging in size from 1-2 Mb to larger 5-15 Mb domains. The interaction sites were reproducible across replicates and clustered in a characteristic manner at 16 and 20 hpi distinct from early (12 hpi) and late (24 hpi) infection.
results.evaluation: Claims C59, C61-C63, C68-C69 are supported by V3C-seq data across the mouse genome (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and 2). The size ranges of VADs are clearly observable in the data (C61-C62), and clustering analysis demonstrates reproducibility and characteristic temporal patterns (C68-C69). The observation that some chromosomes have fewer interaction sites (C63) is evident in the genome-wide data.

results.result: At later time points (20-24 hpi), MVM interaction patterns changed, with fewer sites retained from 16 hpi (~39%) and fewer newly generated sites (~18%). By 24 hpi, interactions were extensive throughout the genome, likely reflecting saturating viral DNA levels, substantial cellular DNA damage, and viral packaging reducing available genomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67, C71-C75 are supported by time-course V3C-seq data (Figure 2B-C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2). The quantitative analysis of VAD retention and generation (C66-C67) is clear. The interpretation that late-stage widespread interaction reflects saturation and loss of specificity (C72-C73) is reasonable. The caveats about cellular DNA damage (C74) and viral packaging (C75) are appropriately noted and supported by data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) and citation, respectively.

results.result: In human NB324K cells at 16 hpi, MVM localized to the human fragile site FRA5H but not FRA11F, and associated weakly with the prototypical fragile site FRA3B, demonstrating that MVM can associate with fragile sites in human cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C113 are supported by focused 3C-qPCR in human NB324K cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). The differential association with different fragile sites (strong with FRA5H, weak with FRA3B, none with FRA11F) is clearly shown. This extends the findings to human cells, though the data are limited to a single time point and cell type.

results.result: Genome-wide analysis of γ-H2AX ChIP-seq revealed that approximately 55% of sites in mock-infected cells overlapped with 16 hpi, with 55% of 16 hpi sites newly generated. By 16 hpi, close to 90% of γ-H2AX sites overlapped with VADs, decreasing to ~70% by 20 hpi due to increased cellular DNA breaks. Random peak controls showed <1% overlap.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86, C96-C99, C102 are supported by quantitative analysis of γ-H2AX ChIP-seq and V3C-seq data (Figure 3B-D). The percentages are clearly calculated and presented, with appropriate statistical controls (C102). The interpretation that decreased overlap at 20 hpi reflects increased DNA damage (C99) is supported by the data showing widespread damage induction (C89-C90). The heatmap analysis (C98, Figure 3D) provides additional visualization of the temporal dynamics.

results.result: Comparison with published chromatin marks suggests MVM associations may be with the A compartment of TADs, which would provide necessary machinery for expression and replication. Host chromatin states may play a significant role in permissiveness to DNA damage and MVM localization, with regions in protective chromatin environments potentially providing supportive conditions for infection.
results.evaluation: Claims C176-C177, C184-C187 involve comparisons with published chromatin data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E) and integration with literature on chromatin environments. While the overlay with Type A chromatin marks (C176) is shown, the interpretation that MVM associates with the A compartment (C176-C177) is tentative ('suggests', 'may be'). The broader speculation about chromatin states and permissiveness (C184, C187) is reasonable but not directly tested. These claims represent plausible hypotheses requiring further investigation.

results.result: HU pretreatment of permissive rat F111 cells, which have lower levels of endogenous DNA damage (lower γ-H2AX), resulted in increased MVM replication by 20 hpi, consistent with the model that pre-existing DNA damage sites facilitate MVM replication.
results.evaluation: Claims C190-C191 are supported by immunoblot data (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B) showing increased NS1 levels (indicating increased replication) in HU-pretreated F111 cells. The observation that F111 cells have lower baseline γ-H2AX (C191) is shown in the same figure. This result supports the overall model, though it is based on a single experiment in one cell type.

results.result: The model proposed for parvovirus infection differs from adenovirus, as the parvovirus life cycle depends on cell cycle arrest, is susceptible to ATM inhibitors, continually induces DNA damage, is more dependent on host factors, and lacks extensive genetic capacity to inactivate the cellular DDR.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C152 distinguish the MVM model from adenovirus based on established knowledge about parvovirus biology (C148-C150, supported by prior citations) and known differences in genetic capacity (C151-C152, supported by citations). The distinction (C147) is appropriate and helps contextualize the findings. These claims are primarily interpretive and rely on established knowledge rather than new data from this study.

results.result: V3C-seq offers advantages over existing methods (ChIA-PET and Hi-C) for mapping virus-host interactions. A single inverse-PCR viewpoint is sufficient for MVM, ensuring detection of only MVM-host hybrid junctions with higher resolving power and deeper interrogation. However, V3C-seq does not assay changes in nuclear architecture in response to infection.
results.evaluation: Claims C153-C161 compare V3C-seq to existing methods based on published work (C153-C156, supported by citations) and describe methodological advantages (C158-C160) demonstrated in the study. The limitation regarding nuclear architecture (C161) is appropriately acknowledged. The comparison is fair and the advantages are demonstrated by the data, though direct head-to-head comparisons with other methods are not performed.

results.result: Background information on parvoviruses, MVM biology, DNA damage response, fragile sites, other viruses, chromosome conformation capture technologies, TADs, and relevant prior work establishes the context and rationale for the study.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C37, C46, C48, C52, C140-C146, C172-C175, C180-C182 represent established knowledge and prior work, appropriately cited throughout. These claims provide necessary background and context for understanding the significance of the study. They are supported by appropriate citations and represent accurate summaries of the literature.

results.result: The V3C-seq assay should be useful for characterizing interactions of many DNA viruses with the cellular genome and for studying long-range interactions of integrated viruses, providing a tool to characterize molecular events leading to infection initiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C45, C188, C189, and C166 are speculative statements about future applications of V3C-seq. While the method is well-validated for MVM, its applicability to other viruses has not been demonstrated in this study. The speculation is reasonable given the general nature of the approach, but remains untested. These represent hypotheses for future work rather than supported conclusions.

results.result: The authors acknowledge important limitations: it cannot be formally ruled out that early VAD sites were virally-induced rather than pre-existing; γ-H2AX may be directly associated with viral genomes; and specific localization of input genomes remains circumstantial as multiple genomes have accumulated even at early time points.
results.evaluation: Claims C104, C192-C193, C196-C197 represent appropriate acknowledgments of limitations and alternative interpretations. These caveats are important for accurate interpretation of the results and demonstrate scientific rigor. The authors correctly note that while the data strongly support their model, certain aspects remain inferential rather than definitively proven.
